datacenters.name: CATAC
datacenters.summary: The Central American Tsunami Advisory Center (CATAC) established at INETER, Managua, Nicaragua, provides tsunami services for the Central American countries (Nicaragua, Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras, Costa Rica, Panama) within the framework of IOC/UNESCO (Pacific Tsunami Warning System PTWS and Caribbean Tsunami Warning System CARIBE TWS). It receives seismic waveform data in real time from around 500 seismic stations in Central America and surrounding areas. It detects and characterizes earthquakes and identifies the possible generation of tsunami. The possible impact of the tsunami is evaluated with geophysical and oceanographic methods and parameters like tsunami arrival time and amplitudes are predicted and communicated to the scientific and civil protection institutions responsible for tsunamis warning in the Central American countries.

datacenters.name: GEOSHAKE
datacenters.summary:
GeoShake operates the data services for the GW network, a citizen seismic network of low-cost MEMS accelerometer stations hosted by private individuals.
All data is served anonymously under CC BY 4.0: no registration, no API key and no rate agreement. A public limit of 100 requests per 5 minutes per IP applies purely as abuse protection and is not an access restriction.

Two standard services are live: fdsnws-station (StationXML 1.1, including level=response with a nominal instrument sensitivity) and fdsnws-event (QuakeML 1.2). Real-time continuous and triggered waveforms are available over SeedLink at seedlink.geoshake.org:18000, and individual triggers can be downloaded as SAC from the station pages.

fdsnws-dataselect is not implemented yet, so this data centre cannot currently serve archived waveform windows through the standard FDSN route. We would rather leave the field empty than advertise an endpoint that returns 404.

datacenters.name: IESDMC
datacenters.fullName: Institute of Earth Sciences, Academia Sinica, Taiwan
datacenters.summary:
In mid-1992, along with several domestic and foreign institutions, began to prepare a prospectus for establishing a broadband seismic network in the Taiwan region. The network, later named "Broadband Array in Taiwan for Seismology (BATS)," is initially designed with 15 permanent stations located on Taiwan and the surrounding islands, covering an area of approximately 350 km by 400 km. Currently the number of permanent broadband stations operated by IES is 35, including 2 located in the South China Sea with satellite transmission.

 The BATS instrumentation is designed to cover a variety of research demands. All permanent stations are equipped with state-of-the-art very-broadband and strong-motion sensors and 24/26-bits digital recorders. Data streams with high sampling rates (100 sps) were recorded in triggering mode before Q330 was used. After 2002, we gradually upgrade the dataloggers to gain the ability to continuously record ground motion at high sample rates. All stations are capable of internet connection for immediate retrieval of real-time data. We fully take advantage of the Antelope software platform to operate the BATS data acquisition in the data center since 2007. Preliminary data quality control is performed at IES. Afterwards, the data are distributed to the public through the web-based data service at the official BATS website.

We have setup the IES Data Management Center (DMC-IES) which is taking care of the routine network operation, data processing, quality control, and data release, exchange, and contribution etc. The whole dataset is accessible at http://tecws1.earth.sinica.edu.tw/BATSWS in addition to the FDSN Web Service.

datacenters.name: USP
datacenters.fullName: Centro de Sismologia da Universidade de São Paulo
datacenters.summary: The USP Seismological Center coordinate a data center as a result of the collaboration from two distinct institutes in the University, the Instituto de Astronomia, Geofísica e Ciências Atmosféricas (IAG) and Instituto de Energia e Meio Ambiente (IEE), both from Universidade de São Paulo, located in the city of São Paulo, Brazil. The center receives real time data from permanent and temporary stations mainly located in the Central, South and Southeast Brazil. It is a main contributor to the Brazilian Seismographic Network. Additional to own data, USP data center archives data from stations located in the north region of Brazil, as a agreement with the Observatório Sismológico from Universidade de Brasília.
